newsitem.title: USA: RTRS-Golf-Skip Kendall leads Doral Open, Norman tied for second.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Golf-Skip Kendall leads Doral Open, Norman tied for second.

text.p: Skip Kendall, playing in the last group of the day, had the best score of the first round of the Doral Open Thursday, his seven-under-par 65 giving him a one-stroke lead over three golfers.
At six-under 66 were three-time Doral winner Greg Norman, Bob Tway and Lee Rinker.
Five players were at five under par, including the long-slumping 1988 Masters winner Sandy Lyle, off to his best tournament start in years.

Kendall had eight birdies in the first 12 holes of Doral's Blue course. "I didn't want to get ahead of myself," he said. "I just wanted to stay focused and hit good shots. The tv cameras started coming out then, and I hit it in a few bunkers coming in."
Kendall's only bogey came on the 16th hole, when he hit into two different bunkers.

Kendall regained his PGA Tour card this year with a ninth-place finish on the 1996 Nike Tour money list. A good showing on the West Coast this year raised his exempt status and allowed him to get into this field, the strongest of the year so far.
Norman not only has won here three times, he also holds the scoring record at 26 under par.

In part because the scoring has been low in recent years, the course was reworked by Raymond Floyd last year, with many new bunkers added and the final hole, the famed Blue Monster, restored to its old level of difficulty.
An atypical lack of wind on Thursday produced scores that did not completely reflect the added difficulty. The field's scoring average was just below par at 71.96.
"One thing about the renovations is that Raymond never changed any of the lines off the tees. I just hit the ball exactly the way I've done in all the years I've been coming here," said Norman.
"There wasn't one shot I was apprehensive on, because I knew exactly where the lines were and where the ball would go," said Norman after his bogey-free round.
